note: Maryland reports abuse to the local department of social services or to local police rather than to a single statewide intake, though 1-800-91-PREVENT will take the call. It also licenses Residential Child Care programs as their own category through the Department of Human Services. One useful piece of Maryland law: since October 2016, where a local department believes a mandated reporter knowingly failed to report, it must file a complaint with that reporter's own licensing board.

civil_injury.summary: Three years from the injury for battery, false imprisonment and negligence. A claim for assault alone (a threat without physical contact) has only one year.
civil_injury.quote: A civil action at law shall be filed within three years from the date it accrues unless another provision of the Code provides a different period of time within which an action shall be commenced.
civil_injury.note: § 5-105: 'An action for assault, libel, or slander shall be filed within one year from the date it accrues.' (https://mgaleg.maryland.gov/mgawebsite/Laws/StatuteText?article=gcj&section=5-105&enactments=false). Battery is not named in § 5-105 and falls under the three-year general period; a lawyer should plead battery where there was physical contact.

civil_minor_tolling.summary: For someone injured as a child, the clock starts at 18: three years for battery or negligence (so by the 21st birthday), and one year for assault alone. There is no longer deadline for non-sexual physical abuse of a child.
civil_minor_tolling.quote: When a cause of action subject to a limitation under Subtitle 1 of this title ... accrues in favor of a minor or mental incompetent, that person shall file his action within the lesser of three years or the applicable period of limitations after the date the disability is removed.
civil_minor_tolling.note: The 'lesser of' wording means the one-year assault period stays one year after 18. The special child abuse provision (§ 5-117) covers sexual abuse only and was not researched.

civil_government_claims.summary: Against the State: a written claim to the State Treasurer within 1 year of the injury, and suit within 3 years. Against a county or city: written notice within 1 year of the injury under the Local Government Tort Claims Act.
civil_government_claims.citation: Md. Code, State Gov't § 12-106; Cts. & Jud. Proc. § 5-304
civil_government_claims.quote: the claimant submits a written claim to the Treasurer or a designee of the Treasurer within 1 year after the injury to person or property that is the basis of the claim; (2) the Treasurer or designee denies the claim finally; and (3) the action is filed within 3 years after the cause of action arises.
civil_government_claims.note: Local notice: § 5-304(b)(1) 'notice of the claim required by this section is given within 1 year after the injury' (https://mgaleg.maryland.gov/mgawebsite/Laws/StatuteText?article=gcj&section=5-304&enactments=false). Both allow late notice for good cause if the government was not prejudiced, and neither requires notice if the government had actual or constructive notice within 1 year.

criminal_child_abuse.summary: No time limit. Child abuse by a parent, household member or anyone with care or custody of a minor is a felony in Maryland, and Maryland has no statute of limitations for felonies.
criminal_child_abuse.citation: Md. Code, Crim. Law § 3-601; Cts. & Jud. Proc. § 5-106(a)
criminal_child_abuse.quote: A parent or other person who has permanent or temporary care or custody or responsibility for the supervision of a minor may not cause abuse to the minor.
criminal_child_abuse.note: No statute states 'no limit' for felonies; § 5-106 sets limits for misdemeanors only, and felonies are prosecutable at any time under Maryland common law. § 3-601(d)(2): a violator 'is guilty of the felony of child abuse in the second degree and on conviction is subject to imprisonment not exceeding 15 years'; first degree (death or severe physical injury) is a felony with up to 25 years.

criminal_felony_assault.summary: No time limit for first degree assault, a felony. Second degree assault is a misdemeanor; ordinary misdemeanors must be charged within one year, but Maryland exempts misdemeanors that can be punished with a penitentiary sentence, and whether second degree assault falls under that exemption is not settled here.
criminal_felony_assault.citation: Md. Code, Crim. Law §§ 3-202, 3-203; Cts. & Jud. Proc. § 5-106(a)
criminal_felony_assault.quote: Except as provided by this section, § 1-303 of the Environment Article, and § 8-1815 of the Natural Resources Article, a prosecution for a misdemeanor shall be instituted within 1 year after the offense was committed.
criminal_felony_assault.note: First degree assault (§ 3-202) is 'the felony of assault in the first degree'. Second degree assault (§ 3-203) is 'the misdemeanor of assault in the second degree' with up to 10 years' imprisonment. § 5-106(b) removes the limit for misdemeanors a statute makes punishable 'in the penitentiary'; § 3-203 does not say that, so the one-year limit appears to apply, but this was not confirmed against case law.

channels.name: Maryland Board of Professional Counselors and Therapists
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and disciplines professional counselors and therapists, including marriage and family therapists and alcohol and drug counselors. Where the Board votes to investigate, it assigns its own investigator, and a thorough investigation has to come before any charge against a licensee.
channels.what_it_cannot_do: It says many financial and interpersonal issues fall outside its jurisdiction because no breach of the Professional Counselors Act is involved. It cannot help you sue for money or settle a fee dispute.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed counselor or therapist in Maryland. Psychologists and social workers have separate boards.
channels.how: File through the Board's complaint gateway. Complaints are taken from patients, family members and any other member of the public.

channels.name: Maryland Board of Examiners of Psychologists
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and disciplines psychologists and registered psychology associates in Maryland.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed psychologist or registered psychology associate.
channels.how: Complete the Board's complaint form - there are separate written instructions for filling it in - and send it to the Board.

channels.name: Maryland DHS, Licensing and Monitoring (Residential Child Care)
channels.what_it_can_do: Licenses and monitors Residential Child Care programs in Maryland as a distinct category, and takes complaints about them.
channels.who_to_report: A licensed residential child care program.
channels.how: Contact the Department of Human Services.

channels.name: Maryland child abuse and neglect reporting
channels.what_it_can_do: Starts a child protective services investigation. Reports go to the local department of social services for the county the child is in, or to local law enforcement.
channels.who_to_report: A child at a Maryland program.
channels.how: Call the local department of social services, or 1-800-91-PREVENT, or 911 in an emergency. Report orally straight away; a mandated reporter must also file a written report within 48 hours.

channels.name: Disability Rights Maryland
channels.what_it_can_do: Maryland's Protection and Advocacy agency, with federal authority to investigate abuse and neglect of people with disabilities in facilities, a right of access to them, and free legal advocacy.
channels.who_to_report: A Maryland program where the young person has a disability or a mental health diagnosis.
